questions.problem:
An ambulance service helicopter takes off from a hospital helipad three times on a particular day. The helicopter's location a few seconds after these takeoffs are given by points $P,$ $Q,$ and $R.$

questions.worked_solution:
Remember that in general, if a point $A$ has coordinates $({a}_{x},{a}_{y},{a}_{z}),$ then its position vector is given by

$$
\overset{\to }{OA}=⟨{a}_{x},{a}_{y},{a}_{z}⟩.
$$

Here, the point $P$ has coordinates $(0,0,3),$ so its position vector is given by

$$
\begin{aligned}p & =⟨0,0,3⟩.\end{aligned}
$$

The point $Q$ has coordinates $(0,-3,2),$ so its position vector is given by

$$
\begin{aligned}q & =⟨0,-3,2⟩.\end{aligned}
$$

The point $R$ has coordinates $(0,4,3),$ so its position vector is given by

$$
\begin{aligned}r & =⟨0,4,3⟩.\end{aligned}
$$

questions.worked_solution:
The magnitude of a vector $a$ with components $⟨{a}_{x},{a}_{y},{a}_{z}⟩$  can always be computed as

$$
\begin{aligned}|\,a\,| & =\sqrt{{a}_{x}^{2}+{a}_{y}^{2}+{a}_{z}^{2}}.\end{aligned}
$$

From part 1, we have $q=⟨0,-3,2⟩$ and $r=⟨0,4,3⟩.$ Therefore,

$$
\begin{aligned}|\,q\,| & =\sqrt{{0}^{2}+(-3)^{2}+{2}^{2}} \\  & =\sqrt{0+9+4} \\  & =\sqrt{13},\end{aligned}
$$

and

$$
\begin{aligned}|\,r\,| & =\sqrt{{0}^{2}+{4}^{2}+{3}^{2}} \\  & =\sqrt{0+16+9} \\  & =\sqrt{25} \\  & =5.\end{aligned}
$$

From part 3, we also have $x=⟨0,7,1⟩.$ This gives

$$
\begin{aligned}|\,x\,| & =\sqrt{{0}^{2}+{7}^{2}+{1}^{2}} \\  & =\sqrt{0+49+1} \\  & =\sqrt{50} \\  & =5\sqrt{2}.\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, $|\,q\,|=\sqrt{13}$, $|\,r\,|=5$ and $|\,x\,|=5\sqrt{2}.$

The dot product of two vectors given in component form can be computed by summing up the products of corresponding components of vectors:

$$
\begin{aligned}q\cdot r & ={q}_{x}\cdot {r}_{x}+{q}_{y}\cdot {r}_{y}+{q}_{z}\cdot {r}_{z}\end{aligned}

questions.worked_solution:
To find the angle $\theta $ between the vectors, we can rearrange the dot product formula:

$$
\begin{aligned}q\cdot r & =|\,q\,|\cdot |\,r\,|\cdot \operatorname{cos}⁡\theta  \\ \operatorname{cos}⁡\theta  & =\frac{q\cdot r}{|\,q\,||\,r\,|}\end{aligned}

From part 4, we have $|\,q\,|=\sqrt{13}$ and $|\,r\,|=5.$ Also, from part 5, we have $q\cdot r=-6.$ Therefore, 

$$
\begin{aligned}\operatorname{cos}⁡\theta  & =\frac{q\cdot r}{|\,q\,||\,r\,|} \\  & =\frac{(-6)}{\sqrt{13}\cdot 5} \\  & =-\frac{6}{5\sqrt{13}}\end{aligned}
$$

Finally,

$$
\theta =\operatorname{arccos}⁡(-\frac{6}{5\sqrt{13}})≈{109}^{∘}.
$$
